Welcome to Lorenden Prep School
Lorenden Prep School is a gem, tucked away in an enviable location but yet within easy reach of Faversham. Pupils age 3-11 benefit from small class sizes, expert teaching, lots of open space and access to the forty acres of woodland Trustlands directly behind the school. We are the only ISI top-rated ‘Excellent’ Prep School in Swale. Visit us and see how your children could thrive in this rich environment.

Inspection reports
Share this page
We are delighted to share our most recent inspection report from the Independent Schools Inspectorate, following their visit to Lorenden in June 2023. This was a Regulatory Compliance Inspection, in which the inspection team assessed whether we were compliant in eight different sections. As you will see, we successfully met all standards in each of these eight main areas.
Lorenden's previous ISI inspection took place in November 2018, and focused on Educational Quality. We achieved the very top grading that can be given to schools, that of 'excellent' for both graded categories - academic achievement and personal development.
The report has many superb comments that are still true to this day, and if you haven't got time to read the whole document then please do just peruse some of the highlights we have picked out below.
‘The quality of pupils’ academic and other achievements is excellent.’
‘School leavers are successful in gaining places at senior schools with competitive entry requirements for which they are prepared well. The more able achieve a range of academic, drama, music and sport awards.’
‘Pupils communicate with each other and their teachers with enthusiasm, confidence and eloquent expression…..and express themselves articulately in their speaking and writing.’
‘...teachers encourage pupils to think for themselves and develop independent learning habits by providing stimulating challenge.’
‘...the success achieved in team sports is outstanding.’
‘Pupils demonstrate substantial self-confidence and resilience from the EYFS upwards.’
‘Pupils show a clear sense of the value of positive behaviour, kindness and compassion that is actively promoted by the school.’

Our History
Share this page
Learn about Lorenden
Lorenden Prep School was born out of the passion and perseverance of a group of hardworking staff and parents of the previous Nativity School in Sittingbourne. Seeking premises for a new school this intrepid group set about finding the perfect location for a small, independent school and so Lorenden Prep School was founded at ‘Lorenden’ in Painters’ Forstal. It is a testament to the ongoing community spirit of the school that some founder members of the school still work at Lorenden Prep School today.
Planning permission granted at Lorenden
To great excitement, planning was finally granted in June 1993 to allow the beautiful Georgian house, ‘Lorenden’, in Painter’s Forstal to become an independent Prep School for not more than one hundred and twenty pupils. Work began by the founding members to turn the premises into a suitable educational establishment.
Lorenden opens its doors to pupils for the first time
Over one hundred pupils were on the roll of the school as it opened for the very first time in September 1993, under the direction of their Headmistress, Mrs Anne Hannaford.
Lorenden joins IAPS
Lorenden Prep School's Head becomes a member of the Independent Association of Prep Schools, on behalf of the school. Membership is dependent on the school fulfilling a number of criteria, assuring parents of the quality of the education their child is receiving. Membership, held by the Head on behalf of the school, continues to the present day.
Lorenden opens its new building
In October 2010, The Right Honourable Hugh Robertson MP formally opened the school’s new building which comprised a spacious hall, changing rooms and two further classrooms.
Lorenden joins MIST
Lorenden Prep School joins the Methodist Independent Schools Trust and becomes part of a larger network of schools with a strong sense of caring, an unpretentious approach and a desire for children to grow up as honest and happy individuals. Links become closer with Kent College, Canterbury through this relationship.
Forest School starts at Lorenden
Under the direction of a Forest School qualified member of staff, Forest School begins at the school, using the school’s grounds and the forty acres of Trustlands backing on to the school’s playing fields.
Mrs Kathy Uttley
joins Lorenden Prep School as the Headteacher
25 Years of Lorenden
Lorenden celebrates its twenty-fifth birthday with a range of events, which begun with an exhibition on ‘A History of Lorenden and Painter’s Forstal’ held in the Faversham Fleur de Lis Museum during February. The school is awarded 'Excellent' in all categories in its ISI Inspection.
Mr Richard McIntosh joins as Headteacher

Early Years
Share this page
We are very proud of our Early Years.
We have a dedicated team of qualified teachers striving to ensure that children develop a lifelong love of learning, a healthy curiosity and the ability to ask questions through the freedom of choice and exploration. We recognise the importance of social, emotional and physical development and ensure that each child is nurtured in order to become independent and confident through daily exploration and interaction.
Our Environment
We have fantastic indoor spaces, and a large and exciting Early Years outdoor environment just for Nursery and Reception pupils as well regular use of the school fields and the Lorenden Trustlands beyond. Early Years have lunch with their teachers and Pre-Prep in the generous hall and they love saying hello to other teachers and pupils, who all know who they are, as they go along the corridors!
Literacy and Numeracy
We develop confident learners with enquiring minds, and we have strong emphasis on the acquisition of numeracy and literacy skills. We teach children to read using phonics and then we read with them daily – we expect parents to do their bit too! We structure child-initiated sessions and teacher-led activities using children’s interests. We teach children to write – from the first steps of mark making to little stories – it all happens in the Early Years! We encourage mathematical thinking and teach maths in the ‘mastery’ method that is used by the rest of the school. A recent Early Years advisor that we commissioned to visit, found that pupils’ literacy and numeracy were well developed by the end of their time in the Early Years.
Specialist Teachers in Nursery and Reception
We have specialist teachers for French, Music and PE for both classes. We have weekly Forest School sessions with trained staff too. All Early Years children are part of the Pre-Prep choir and learn to sing songs in one and two parts.
Being part of the whole school
A key part of Lorenden is the buddy system between Year 6 and Reception pupils and between Year 5 and Nursery pupils. Younger pupils have regular opportunities to play and to engage in activities with their older buddies and strong friendships are built across the year groups, helping younger pupils to feel secure, confident and valued in the community and for older pupils to develop their sense of responsibility and kindness further.

Nursery
Share this page
Nursery
Our lovely Nursery for three and four year olds is a warm, friendly, calm and caring setting for your child to learn, grow and make friends. With a maximum of sixteen children per session and two full-time, highly qualified and experienced staﬀ, your child will receive the best care and education as they start their journey towards Reception. We value each child as an individual and provide stimulating activities, resources and experiences that allow everyone to learn, develop, and grow in a meaningful way.
Teaching and Learning in Nursery
In Nursery, we are proud to be an integral part of the whole school community, embracing the Lorenden values: ‘We care, we share, we strive, we succeed.’
Our bright and cheerful classroom, alongside our large and inviting garden, provides two exciting environments for children to explore throughout the day. We promote independence and understand the importance of creating an organised and engaging space where children can confidently access resources on their own. Whether selecting activities from the shelves or helping their teachers prepare the garden for the day, children are encouraged to make choices and take responsibility within their learning environment.
We believe that child-centred learning, combined with a strong emphasis on emotional and social development, fosters self-confidence, high self-esteem, meaningful friendships, and independence. This approach empowers children to embrace challenges and builds a strong foundation for a lifelong love of learning. Communication with parents is extremely important to us. We value the opportunity to greet you at the beginning and end of each day and to share in your child’s experiences. We also use an online learning journal, Tapestry, which allows you to view photos and updates showcasing all the fun and learning taking place during your child’s busy Nursery day. In addition, you will receive a detailed written report twice a year, covering the areas of the Early Years Curriculum.

Sports Department
Share this page
Lorenden PE Aims and Objectives
Lorenden aim to give every child the best sporting opportunity, whilst endeavouring to help each individual fulfil their true potential.
How do we achieve this?
By providing a wide range of sporting disciplines in our purpose built sports hall or our lovely grounds. We believe in achieving this through a committed, professional and caring team of PE and Games staff. The Games Department is currently divided into two sections, Boys’ Games and Girls’ Games whilst PE is be taught in year groups.
Facilities
The school boasts a purpose built sports hall with modern changing room facilities and underfloor heating. Also we have the infamous and picturesque Lorenden grounds which holds our sports field comprising of U9 and U11 pitches. We also have access to acres of trust land where orienteering and cross-country is held. Closer to the school there is a hard court area used for tennis, netball and hockey throughout the year. We have affiliation and links with local facilities providing us with an astro-turf and a swimming pool.
Pre Prep
A new and exciting development has been the design and implementation of structured PE in the Pre-Prep area of the school. At Lorenden, we believe that providing a structured yet fun approach to sport at a young age can only help each child to develop greater sporting talents at a faster rate. This also allows the school to have a uniform method of teaching PE from Nursery through to Year 6.
PE lessons
We run PE classes throughout Lorenden, with all pupils in pre prep having two lessons a week and prep pupils having one lesson a week with additional four games lessons and fixtures.
The PE Curriculum
This includes but is not limited to: Gymnastics, Coordination and Skills sessions, Health Related Fitness, Cross-Country, OAA, Dance, Badminton, Athletics, Basketball, Short Tennis, Volleyball, Hockey and Inclusive or Adapted Sports.
Matches, age groups, Games sessions
We understand that not everyone finds all sports easy to learn but we play against a range of local prep and primary schools of differing abilities. Every term we select boys and girls to represent the school in two age groups of U9’s and U11’s. Where possible and when numbers permit we try to provide two teams at each fixture, it is a target of the school that in the near future the U11’s will go on a sports tour. Every child at Lorenden has the opportunity to represent the school at fixtures which exemplifies our aim as a PE and Games department. The captains are asked to write and read out their match reports after each match in the Achievement assembly to encourage their public speaking and team spirit, while also informing the rest of the school about their achievements.
Sporting Choices
We offer a wide variety of activities throughout each academic year. On offer for the boys is football, rugby, cricket, short-tennis, badminton, athletics, cross-country, hockey and swimming. Girls’ sports include rounders, hockey, netball, badminton, swimming, cross- country and athletics. However, if there are specific needs and talents of children we will endeavour to support them in training and competition where possible.
Trials
As children begin to show a higher level of ability and attainment in specific sports, we will look to enrol them in district and county school trials. If further selected, we endeavour to support them in regional and national selection processes.
Scholarships
Annually we advise, support and facilitate students with excellent sporting talent in their quest to achieve Sports Scholarships to top Senior Schools within the Independent schools sector.
Clubs
There are a fantastic range of sporting clubs to choose from at Lorenden for any age or gender: Football, Rugby, Archery, Cricket, Dodgeball, Kwik Cricket, Multi Sports, Multi Skills, Netball, Hockey, Rounders, Taekwondo and Cross-Country. However, if there are sports that have interest from pupils, and we do not yet offer, we endeavour to provide our pupils with the opportunity to participate in them.
Our Ethos
We understand that sport crosses cultures, bridges gaps, builds a sense of community and adds to the well-being of a child’s school life. We strongly believe that what we teach the children on Lorenden will prepare them fully for the diverse and challenging sporting environment of senior school. We hope that each individual child can be celebrated here, finding their niche and learning to love and enjoy sport whilst maintaining a healthy mind and body before departing.
For more information, please do not hesitate to contact the school.

About our school
Share this page
Lorenden Prep School is an "excellent" ISI graded school; a gem, tucked away in an enviable location but yet within easy reach of Faversham. Pupils benefit from open playing fields for playtimes as well as sports pitches and access to the forty acres of woodland Trustlands directly behind the school. Visit us and see how your children could thrive in this rich environment.
Introduction from the Head
First and foremost we believe that children need to be happy in order to learn and from the moment you step inside the school you can sense the friendly community that allows pupils to blossom.
We expect good manners, kindness and perseverance from everyone and our motto “We Care. We Share. We Strive. We Succeed.” underpins everything we do.
Read the Head’s Welcome
Approach to learning
Walk into any classroom at Lorenden and you will see children enjoying and engaging with their learning. With small class sizes, teachers get to know pupils very quickly.
We have a strong record of pupils being awarded Grammar school places and in pupils receiving offers for a range of Independent School scholarships including Academic, Sport, Drama and Music.
Inspection reports
We are delighted to share our latest inspection report from November 2018 which covers Educational Quality and Focused Compliance.
We have achieved the very top grading that can be given to schools, that of 'excellent' for both graded categories - academic achievement and personal development. We are also fully compliant.
Read inspection reports
Our Team
Our team are all friendly and professional people who want the best for pupils at Lorenden. Highly qualified teachers are supported by excellent teaching assistants and support staff. The staff at Lorenden are a true team and together exemplify the behaviours expected of pupils. Parents and pupils are made to feel really welcome and staff make every effort to get to know each child in the school.
Get to know the team
We love the family atmosphere at Lorenden. The staff genuinely care about the children and our kids have blossomed with the attention and encouragement they receive. As parents we always feel welcome to pop in and that our thoughts and suggestions are listened to. We're looking forward to our third child joining the lovely caring community at Lorenden next year.

Introduction from the Head
Share this page
Lorenden has supported me to achieve things I never thought I’d achieve.
I am thrilled to have been entrusted with the privilege of leading Lorenden Prep School. From the moment you arrive at our school you can sense the happy and friendly atmosphere, both in and out of the classroom, that allows pupils to blossom. As I greet our families at the gate each morning, the sight of our pupils smiling and even running or skipping into school brings joy to the heart. Our team here believe that children need to be happy in order to learn well and have the best possible school experience. As the late Rita Pierson once said: "Kids don't learn from people that they don't like."
It has been fascinating to talk to our parents about why they chose Lorenden for their children. A number of reasons emerged, whether it is our happy family atmosphere where children gain confidence to be themselves, our fabulous Early Years environment, our small class sizes, Forest School, successful Kent Test preparation or strong sports teams. We welcome all pupils to our fantastic school.
Lorenden pupils develop into self-disciplined, thoughtful children with a cheerful ‘can do’ attitude to life and a strong sense of fair play. We prepare them socially, physically and intellectually for secondary education and leave them with happy memories of their time with us. One parent told me recently that they wanted their child to have as close to an idyllic childhood as possible, and attending Lorenden was integral to that.
At Lorenden everyone is happy and wants to learn.
We expect good manners, kindness and perseverance from everyone and our philosophy of “We Care. We Share. We Strive. We Succeed.” underpins everything that we do. Strong pastoral care is key to our success; we consistently reinforce positive behaviour with the reward of house points and 'gems' which are celebrated in assemblies each week.
Lorenden will always make you feel welcome whether it is your first day or your last.
We are delighted that most of our pupils join Lorenden because of a recommendation from a current or previous parent. Younger siblings are invariably always enrolled once an older brother or sister has joined. We also attract parents who move into the area, often from London, who desire an ideal school that has high academic standards alongside a caring, family environment.
Being a community and a family is very important to us. New pupils across the school and their parents are made to feel very welcome – even pupils visiting for taster days do not want to leave!
We have extremely strong sports teams in the Prep School, offer a wide range of individual music lessons and small musical ensembles and are proud that pupils of all ages feel confident to perform solos in whole school assemblies. Our choir performs at key events throughout the year and a large scale production each summer showcases a wealth of dramatic talent.
I would be delighted to show you around our wonderful school soon.
We love the family atmosphere at Lorenden. The staff genuinely care about the children and our kids have blossomed with the attention and encouragement they receive. As parents we always feel welcome to pop in and that our thoughts and suggestions are listened to. We're looking forward to our third child joining the lovely caring community at Lorenden next year.
Year 1 and Year 3 parent
Richard McIntosh, Head of Lorenden Prep School
